But you're leaving out that if a motorists checks for cyclists in their mirror and blind spot before turning and sees that they will not hit one, then they are free to signal and turn. They are not in the wrong simply because they caused a cyclist to slow. If a cyclist runs into them, then that's the cyclist's fault, because the cyclist was fully able to slow, but chose not to.

Lets take cyclists out of the equation. A car and a truck are driving down the street. The car is in the left lane and the truck is in the right. The car is ahead of the truck. The car needs to change into the right lane and then turn right at the next intersection. The car checks their mirror and blind spot and see that they're far enough ahead of the truck that they will not hit the truck. The car signals and then moves into the right lane in front of the truck. The car has left enough room so that when it pulls into that lane and slows for the turn the truck has enough space so that they will have enough reaction time and space to not hit the car. The car then slows for the turn, causing the truck to slow.

The truck doesn't have the right to plow into the car. The car made a legal lane change and a legal turn. The car made sure to signal, check mirrors, and blind spot. Yes the car caused the truck to slow or even stop, but that doesn't give the truck the right to plow into the car. The truck had more than enough space and time to slow.

If someone is turning in front of you, signals, and gives you more than enough time to slow, then you're in the wrong if there's an accident. Yes they will be impeding the traffic in your lane, but if they stop and wait for you to go past, then they're causing traffic in their lane to slow or stop, instead of causing you to slow or stop. And they shouldn't impede one lane's traffic for another's traffic. If they can turn without hitting you and you have enough room and time to slow, then that is what they are required to do (even if your lane has more traffic).

So yes, "the DMV instructs motorists to check for cyclists in their mirror and blind spot before turning". They're instructed to check and make sure they don't hit them, vehicles may still cause cyclists to slow, just like they will cause other vehicles to slow. Cyclists don't have the right of way simply because they're cyclists.
